newsitem.title: USA: Prince George's County okays sports complex -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Prince George's County okays sports complex -- paper.

text.p: The Prince George's County Council, Md., approved on Tuesday $31 million in spending for the construction of a community sports complex next to a new Redskins stadium, the Washington Post reported Wednesday.
The measure, approved unanimously by the council, allows the Maryland-National Capital Park and Planning Commission to spend the funds in the next year, the Post reported.

The approval and fast track action is an unprecedented move for the county planners, who typically take several years to fund and build large projects, the paper reported. The commission had planned to spend the money over six years.
The council describes the sports complex as a much-needed facility for the disadvantaged young people inside the Beltway, the Post reported.

The $31 million in public funds will pay for a field house that includes a 200-meter track, a fitness center, a gymnasium and an aquatic facility with a 50-meter pool. It would take an additional $20 million in private money to complete even bigger plans for an ice rink, golf course and tennis court.
The Redskins contributed $3 million to jump-start the sports complex; the county contributed the $4.1 million it made from the sale of the stadium site.

County officials said they hope the sports complex will spur revitalization of the Landover area, which so far has been slow to fell any positive effects from the stadium's development, the Post reported.
